summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson was admitted for dizziness, shortness of breath, and chest pain. His dizziness was attributed to dehydration from a recent increase in furosemide, which resolved with IV fluids. Workup revealed significant weight loss, elevated inflammatory markers, liver enzyme abnormalities, myalgias, and a restrictive lung pattern on PFTs. After multidisciplinary evaluation, a preliminary diagnosis of amiodarone toxicity was made. Amiodarone and atorvastatin were discontinued, and a short course of prednisone was initiated for lung inflammation. He improved clinically, with stable vital signs and ambulation. Discharge planning included follow-up with pulmonology, hepatology, cardiology, and a chest CT to monitor for amiodarone-induced lung injury. He was discharged home in stable condition with clear medication instructions and outpatient appointments scheduled.
